evidence.reason: In switch(), render(root, overlay) produces the live config bytes ('current'), and record() writes 'switch-before' with those bytes. Immediately after, git restore -- CONFIG reverts the live file to the committed (overlay-less) bytes and then git checkout --detach target runs. If the checkout (or the intervening cleanliness check) fails, the function raises before the later atomic_bytes(root / CONFIG, destination) re-renders the file, so the live host config is left at committed bytes while HEAD is still 'previous'. A retry recomputes current = render(root, overlay) and calls drift_check(current, root / CONFIG), which now mismatches the reverted live file and fails, so the switch cannot be retried without manual intervention. This is an incomplete rollback in the existing atomic-switch behavior, not a request to add a new requirement; writing 'current' back on failure is a small, safe correctness repair (no owner decision needed since normal behavior is unchanged). The defect is at the restore/checkout sequence currently at lines 749-752.
